subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The UK Behavioural Insights Team
description: A 60-second lesson on The UK Behavioural Insights Team.

hook.text: In 2010, the UK created a small team to apply psychology to policy. Critics called it the nudge unit. It saved billions.

buildup.text: The Behavioural Insights Team tested small interventions: rewriting letters, changing forms, and simplifying processes.

discovery.text: One letter change increased tax payments by millions. Adding a line about most neighbors paying on time lifted.

twist.text: The team was expected to fail within a year. Instead it became a global model.

climax.text: Small changes produce large effects when applied at government scale. Behavioral policy proves that design, not force.

punchline.text: A single sentence in a tax letter saved millions of pounds.

quiz.question: How did the UK Behavioural Insights Team increase tax payments?
options: By increasing penalties for late payment
By adding a line saying most neighbors had already paid

details.summary: The UK Behavioural Insights Team, established in 2010, was the world's first government nudge unit. It pioneered the application of behavioral science to policy, running over 750 randomized controlled trials and inspiring more than 200 similar units worldwide.
details.whyItMatters: The BIT proved that behavioral science could be practically applied to government at scale. Its model of small, testable, evidence-based interventions transformed how governments worldwide approach policy design.
takeaways: The BIT was the world's first government nudge unit, founded in 2010
It has run over 750 randomized controlled trials across policy domains
Its success inspired more than 200 similar units in governments worldwide

faq.question: What was the BIT's most famous success?
faq.answer: The tax letter experiment that added social norms messaging increased on-time payment by 15 percent, generating 210 million pounds in additional revenue. Its simplicity and massive return on investment made it the iconic behavioral policy example.

faq.question: How does the BIT test its interventions?
faq.answer: Through randomized controlled trials embedded in normal government operations. Citizens are randomly assigned to receive the standard or modified intervention, and outcomes are compared statistically. Only interventions that prove effective are scaled.
